extraction.summary: Yun and Lee propose a late-time, spatially flat FLRW Einstein-Cartan model with a semiclassical unpolarized Weyssenhoff spin fluid, retaining only a trace-sector torsion scalar Phi. Cartan's equations make torsion algebraically sourced by spin rather than an independent propagating degree of freedom. With radiation neglected and separately conserved dust plus phenomenological holographic dark energy rho_X = 3 d^2 M_p^2 H^2 (Hubble-radius cutoff), the torsion contribution is negative and scales as Phi^2 proportional to a^-6; it shifts the dust-like holographic component to negative w_X and can yield q_0 < 0 without a dark-matter/dark-energy interaction. For fixed Omega_m0 = 0.3, a single Gaussian chi-square fit to the local Pantheon cosmographic q_0 = -1.08 +/- 0.29 gives d_best = 0.924 (+0.007/-0.008); the paper derives |Phi_0/H_0| = 0.392 (+0.016/-0.019) and w_X0 = -1.05 (+0.19/-0.20). This is a one-observable, one-parameter consistency estimate, not a multi-probe or current-data fit. The solution requires z < z_* = 0.249 for E^2 > 0 and |Phi/H| < 1 only to z_wt = 0.194 at that fit; the fitted local interval 0.023-0.15 lies inside both. Separately, using the same background and a torsion-aware geometric-optics/null-bundle calculation for test radiation, the authors derive d_L = d_A (1+z)^2 (1+eta), with weak-torsion eta approximately the line integral of Phi/H. Its plotted absolute magnitude grows with redshift over the same low-z interval. These remain source-level proposals: the background is not extended to early times, perturbations are not treated, the photon stress conservation and test-field assumptions matter, and no distance-duality data are fitted.

ideas.title: Weyssenhoff spin sources an algebraic trace-sector torsion in FLRW
ideas.description: The authors use a semiclassical Weyssenhoff spin fluid with the Frenkel condition, random spin orientation (zero linear spin average but nonzero quadratic average), and a homogeneous/isotropic ansatz restricted to the trace sector S_{mu nu rho} = Phi h_{rho[mu} u_{nu]}. The Cartan equation relates the squared spin density to Phi^2, so Phi is not introduced as an independent propagating field. With their adiabatic particle-number and noninteracting-fluid assumptions, dot(Phi)+3H Phi=0; hence Phi scales as a^-3, while its quadratic contribution to the background scales as a^-6. This is a model closure at homogeneous/isotropic background level; perturbations and microscopic spin dynamics are not developed.

ideas.title: Trace torsion shifts Hubble-cutoff holographic dark energy away from dust
ideas.description: The authors adopt rho_X=3 d^2 M_p^2 H^2 with L=H^-1 and no explicit dark-sector interaction, set Omega_X=d^2, neglect radiation, and separately conserve dust and X. Their derived w_X = -(Phi/H)^2/(1-d^2) for dust is negative for the physical branch, allowing q<0; in the torsion-free limit the noninteracting Hubble-cutoff component returns to dust and does not accelerate. For Omega_m0=0.3, the present constraint requires d >= about 0.837 and the E^2 background exists only for 0 <= z < z_*=0.249 at the quoted fit. The |Phi/H|<1 weak-torsion domain ends earlier at z_wt=0.194. The parameter d -> 0 is outside this physical solution and makes rho_X vanish; the authors explicitly say this is not a continuous LCDM limit because there is no separate cosmological constant. The late-time q comparison fixes Omega_m0=0.3 and fits one parameter to one local cosmographic estimate.

ideas.title: Trace torsion modifies null-bundle reciprocity and luminosity flux
ideas.description: Using the same background, the authors derive a reciprocity correction alpha between source/observer area distances and a path-integrated torsion correction beta to radiation flux, leading to d_L=d_A(1+z)^2(1+eta), eta=sqrt((1+alpha)/(1+beta))-1. For weak torsion alpha is quadratic and dropped at leading order; their trace-sector calculation gives eta approximately integral_0^z [Phi/H] dz/(1+z). They preserve U(1) gauge invariance by taking F=dA, so the Maxwell Lagrangian is affine-connection independent and its spin tensor vanishes. In geometric optics the phase covector is metric-null and its propagation law is written with the full affine covariant derivative, including torsion. They separately assume the canonical radiation stress tensor is covariantly conserved with that connection and treat radiation as a test field decoupled from matter. For the chosen flat-FLRW trace ansatz, the torsion term in the frequency-redshift equation cancels (I=0), leaving a=(1+z)^-1; this is a special result of their ansatz, not asserted for arbitrary torsion. The sign of eta follows the +/- Phi/H branch in Eq. (30); Eq. (51) retains +/- and Fig. 3 displays only |eta|.

caveats: This is explicitly an effective late-time model. Radiation is neglected, the solution fails at z >= z_* for the quoted fit, weak torsion ends at z_wt, and perturbations are out of scope. It cannot establish early-universe or full CMB behavior.

The acceleration result is a one-observable, one-free-parameter consistency estimate: q_0^local is treated as Gaussian, Omega_m0 is fixed at 0.3, and no SNe likelihood, BAO, CC or CMB likelihood/covariance is jointly fit.

The holographic density is adopted phenomenologically from the Hubble-radius cutoff; its microphysical origin remains open in the paper. There is no separate cosmological constant, and d -> 0 is outside the physical solution rather than a recovery of LCDM.

The spin-fluid relation and trace-sector torsion ansatz are model closures. The authors say torsion is algebraically determined by spin, not a propagating scalar, and do not provide perturbation closure or a test of the fluid approximation.

For distance duality, the source assumes radiation is a decoupled test field, its canonical energy-momentum is covariantly conserved using the full affine connection, and emission is isotropic. The result depends on the stated U(1)-preserving F=dA Maxwell prescription and weak-torsion expansion; it is not a fit to observed distance-duality data.

Photon propagation is derived from a metric-null eikonal with a torsion-bearing affine equation (A3), and frequency and beam-area propagation use affine covariant derivatives. The special trace-sector FLRW calculation yields I=0 and the standard a(z) relation; do not generalize that cancellation to arbitrary torsion or silently replace the derivation with a metric-geodesic assumption.
The Phi/H and eta expressions have a +/- sign branch. The paper quotes absolute torsion in its fit and plots |eta|, so the distance-duality sign is not selected by those results.

corrections.locator: Sec.II Eq.(2); Sec.III Eq.(7), Frenkel condition, Eqs.(9),(11)-(12), PDF p.2; HTML #S2.E2,#S3.E7,#S3.E11
corrections.detail: Contracting the displayed Cartan equation at mu=nu gives −2 S_{lambda alpha}{}^alpha=kappa s_{lambda nu}{}^nu. Weyssenhoff s_{lambda nu}{}^nu=s_{lambda nu}u^nu=0 by the stated Frenkel condition. Thus the torsion trace vanishes pointwise. The stated ansatz instead has S_{lambda alpha}{}^alpha=−3Phi u_lambda/2; it forces Phi=0 for this source. Zero linear spin average with nonzero spin² can leave quadratic effective stress, but cannot provide a coherent nonzero trace source or choose its linear sign. Eq.(12) cannot cure this contradiction. The phenomenological negative-stiff background must be kept separate from an accepted Weyssenhoff trace derivation.
